In the past and about 30 years ago, there were no computers or Internet as we have today. At that period, schools weren't provided with technological innovations of our time. The 21st century schools have changed with the development of modern technology and the needs of students. Nowadays, teachers and students use modern technologies. They are using the Internet, computers, laptops, mobiles and a number of other means which are continually being improved and updated. Modern technologies have played a major role in education so that teachers no longer have to rely on their traditional methods of teaching. That's why the concept of a future school comes in. A future school combines high-quality education with the possibility of new technologies in order to convey useful and practical knowledge. Future educators will have to face the fact that students will need to learn in a flexible, personalized format. This may mean having a more technology-focused classroom. In these future schools, students will prefer their learning experience to meet their interests, their academic needs and their future careers. Some of the main features that are expected to be changed in the system of future schools are: flying vehicles instead of school buses, robotic teachers instead of humans, practical work more than books.

The stresses of school life that we are exposed to make us sometimes feel unhappy, depressed, out of control and have low self-esteem. We may feel less motivated in our classrooms or careless about doing homework so that our marks may become low and we don't get good results. Sometimes we find it hard to get up and get ready for school. Some people may hesitate to go to school, or even refuse to go at all. The World Tour Agency said that many people had visited the Iguazu Falls. They told us that the Falls had been so beautiful and could be ranked as one of the ten best places in the world. Tourists said that the Falls they had seen were unique landmarks. They also said that some tourists had found the Falls wonderful with their sub-tropical climate and rains all year. Others said that fresh fruit had been one of the key delights for travellers besides a variety of dishes such as black beans stew, seafood stew and mixed grilled meats. They added that the food at the open market had been good and cheap that tourists decided to have all their meals there. m2: The difference between weather and climate is a measure of time. Weather is what the conditions of the atmosphere are over a short period of time, and climate is how the atmosphere changes over relatively long periods of time. Sometimes the climate differs from one area to another in the same country, for example, Peru has a variety of climate types to choose where to go. It has the blue sky and sunshine of the tropical northern coast, the humid hot Amazon rainforest and the cold weather of the Andes, there is a climate to suit everyone's taste in Peru. On the other hand, some countries have moderate, cold or hot climate all over the year. For example, Portugal enjoys a warm temperate climate with wet winters and dry summers.

What is bullying? Bullying is a repeated, harsh, aggressive behaviour that can be physical, verbal, social or online. You may live in a constant fear of where and when the bullies will strike next, what they will do, and how far they will go. Cyber bullying can occur anywhere. It happens even at home, via smart phones, emails, texts, and social media, 24 hours a day. Cyber bullies use digital technology to annoy, threaten, or humiliate others, unlike traditional bullying which used to occur in streets, school yards or restaurants. Cyber bullying doesn't require face-to-face contact. Bullying can follow you anywhere so that no place, not even home, makes you feel safe. It's important to remember that you're not alone. There are plenty of people who can help you overcome the problem and retain your dignity. How to deal with a bully? There are many ways to deal with a bully. Firstly, you have to keep in mind that there is no simple solution to bullying or cyber bullying. You don't have to blame yourself. It is not your fault, no matter what a bully says or does. The bully is the person with the problem, not you. Secondly, try to find support and encouragement. Talking to a parent, teacher, counselor, or other trusted adults doesn't mean that you're weak. Thirdly, take a break from your smart phone, computer, tablet, and video games. Meet new people and connect with real friends who don't participate in any kind of bullying and who share the same values and interests with you.

m3: Your brain is like a muscle - use it or lose it! The human brain is very small and light (only two percent of our total weight) but it needs about 20% of the oxygen that our body takes in. We can't think well if our brain isn't getting enough oxygen, so always make sure there is enough oxygen in the air when you need to learn or remember something! No one can remember everything, but everyone can learn how to improve their memory. Refresh your memory: The giraffe is trying to ask you something. Decode her message: JEP F EVX JPJB SBJN QB QNE? Albert Einstein, the pioneer of the theory of general relativity, did not even speak until he was 4 years old. By the age of 16, he took an examination for entrance into the Swiss Federal Polytechnic school located in Zurich but failed to earn a passing score. His earlier setbacks did not stop him from winning the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921. After all, he believed that: "Success is failure in progress."

To this day, Albert Einstein is remembered as one of the greatest scientists in history. His story teaches us that failure is not the end; it is only a step on the road to success. If we believe in our dreams and keep working hard, we can achieve them regardless of the obstacles we face.
m5: Elements are represented by chemical symbols. Chemical symbols are a short way of representing the elements. Each symbol consists of one or two letters, usually taken from the element's name. The symbol for the element oxygen is O. The symbol for hydrogen is H and for carbon is C. The symbol for aluminum is Al and for chlorine is Cl. You should note that when two letters are used in a symbol, the first letter is always capitalized but the second letter is never capitalized. Two letters are needed for an element's symbol when the first letter of that element's name has already been used, as the symbol for carbon is C, for calcium is Ca, and for copper is Cu. Scientists often use the Latin name of an element to create its symbol. The symbol for gold is Au. The Latin name for gold is aurum. The symbol for silver is Ag, from the Latin word argentum. The Latin word for iron is ferrum. So the symbol for this element is Fe.

Do you think there is life on other planets? Do you think that creatures on other planets may visit Earth one day? Have you ever seen a spaceship in real life? Well, if you haven't, someone has! In 1947, a pilot named Kenneth Arnold reported seeing nine objects resembling boomerangs in the sky. He described their movement and said that they were "like a saucer if you skip it across the water". This phenomenon is called UFO (unidentified flying object). This term is used to describe any observations of alien spaceships. It is called unidentified because it cannot be immediately explained. Many people believed in that phenomenon, and science-fiction movies started to be made; so we can say that everyone of us has seen a spaceship either in real life or in a movie. However, this phenomenon has been studied by scientists and researchers to clarify the mystery. Researchers think that Arnold probably saw a flock of birds and couldn't tell their exact size, so he didn't know that their large wings created the "V" shape which he described. Other explanations of UFO are that some secret experiments are done by governments under the name of X-Files and so they do not always deny what is presented in movies.

m6: Global warming: is the gradual heating of the Earth's surface, oceans and atmosphere, caused by human activity, primarily the burning of fossil fuels that pump carbon dioxide (CO2), methane and other greenhouse gases into the atmosphere. Global warming and climate change have affected human beings and other creatures. For example: 1 million species of animals and plants face extinction due to climate change and human activity. While we cannot stop global warming overnight, or even over the next several decades, we can slow the rate and limit the amount of global warming by reducing human emissions of heat-trapping gases and black carbon.
